$comment: IntelliSense had no configuration at all, so it fell back to its defaults: C++17,
and no idea where vcpkg's FFmpeg lives. It reported std::span as missing from a tree
that builds -- an error in the editor and nowhere else, which is the worst kind,
because the reflex is to change the code.
The compile database is the fix rather than a hand-written include list: it carries the
exact flags the build used, per file, and stays right when the build changes. CMake
writes it because every preset now sets CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS.
Both databases are listed in one configuration rather than one each. The extension keeps
a single active configuration per folder, so a configuration per subproject meant that
opening a media_server header while smart-video-encoder was selected reported every
include as missing -- again an error only the editor could see. Given several databases
it looks the file up in each, which is what makes the choice unnecessary.
A header is never in a database itself -- IntelliSense infers its flags from a
translation unit that includes it. For the public headers that is exact: the
public_headers_selfcontained target generates one TU per header, so smartvideo/session.h
is read with the same flags the build reads it with.
